subject.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier

question: Should OpenClaw accept `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` as a core config surface now, and what should the no-override legacy behavior mean relative to `minimal`, `standard`, and `full`?
rationale: The source gap is real, but this choice affects public config, prompt context, session state, hook extras, upgrade expectations, and overlapping context-budget controls that automation should not decide.

options.title: Sponsor after contract fixes
options.body: Accept the focused config direction, but require the resolver, help/docs, and tests to distinguish legacy no-override behavior from explicit tier overrides before merge.

options.title: Fold into broader context controls
options.body: Pause this PR and design one context-selection contract that covers tiering, lightweight mode, heartbeat behavior, and hook extras together.

options.title: Decline the new knob
options.body: Close this direction and steer users toward existing bootstrap budgets, `contextInjection`, lightweight context mode, and docs/doctor guidance instead.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after contract fixes
recommendation.body: Accept the focused config direction, but require the resolver, help/docs, and tests to distinguish legacy no-override behavior from explicit tier overrides before merge.
